name: Jones

alpha.desc: The alpha view shows the front of the property from a low elevation angle, revealing a desert terrain setting with scattered juniper and pine trees across the parcel|A rectangular pool structure is visible near the upper-center of the view, and the main residence is partially visible behind dense tree coverage|The long curved driveway approach from the street is partially visible threading through the vegetation toward the structure|Tree density along the front approach limits direct sightlines to the residence from the street.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, with the main residence visible near the center of the parcel surrounded by a landscaped green area|The driveway loop is visible curving around the right side of the structure, and the pool is visible to the upper left of the residence in this perspective|Scattered juniper trees are dense across the right side of the property, narrowing clear access corridors|The terrain is relatively flat near the structure with open desert extending outward.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, which is dominated by open desert terrain with scattered juniper trees and no visible rear structures or access routes|The pool is faintly visible in the upper-right portion of this perspective, and no rear fencing, gates, or improved pathways are visible from this angle|The rear of the parcel transitions directly into undeveloped desert with no defined perimeter barrier visible.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property, with the residence and pool structure visible in the upper-center portion of the frame|A curved driveway is visible on the left side of the structure, and the green lawn area adjacent to the pool is apparent|Dense juniper tree coverage on the left side of the parcel limits lateral sightlines to the structure|No additional detached structures or defined access points are visible from this perspective.

considerations: The residence sits on a large desert parcel accessed by a single curved driveway that loops around the structure, providing a turnaround capability but requiring a long approach through scattered juniper vegetation. The tree canopy and shrub coverage surrounding the residence on all sides reduces direct sightlines from the road and between the structure and property perimeter. The rear of the property has no improved access and transitions to open undeveloped desert. A large pool is located to the north of the residence and represents a notable feature for operational orientation.
clarifications: Is the driveway entrance from Macalpine Loop controlled by a gate or any access barrier? What is the surface material of the driveway — paved, gravel, or compacted dirt — and is it suitable for heavy emergency vehicles? Are there any outbuildings, sheds, or secondary structures on the property not visible from overhead? Is there any exterior address signage visible from the street at the driveway entrance? Does the pool have a surrounding fence or enclosure?
